questions.statement: Which auxiliary verb is essential to form the "going to" future?
questions.context: Identifying the auxiliary for "be going to".

options.feedback: Correct! "Be going to" requires the verb to be conjugated correctly.
Incorrect. "Will" is a separate way to form the future.

questions.explanation:
The student identifies the basic structural component of the "going to" future tense.

questions.statement: Choose the correct question about someone's future intentions.

options.text: What you are going to do?
options.feedback: Incorrect. The verb "be" must come before the subject in a question.

options.text: What are you going to do?
options.feedback: Correct! Standard auxiliary + subject + going to + verb structure.

options.text: What do you going to do?
Are you will go to do?

questions.explanation:
The student understands the word order requirements for questions in the "going to" future.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: According to the list, what is the student's intention regarding video games?
questions.context:
A student's list of intentions.
"My plans for the holidays: 1. I am going to learn to swim. 2. My family is going to travel to Cartagena. 3. I am not going to play video games all day."

options.text: They are going to play more video games.
options.feedback: Incorrect. The list says "not going to".

options.text: They plan to limit or stop playing video games all day.
options.feedback: Correct! The negative intention indicates a plan to avoid that activity.

options.text: They are going to buy new video games in Cartagena.
They are going to play video games only when they swim.
options.feedback: Incorrect. Illogical and not in text.

questions.explanation:
The student applies reading strategies to understand negative intentions in a plan.

questions.statement: "Camilo is studying very hard. He ________ be a doctor when he grows up."

options.feedback: Correct! Shows a firm intention or plan based on his current effort.

questions.statement: Which negative sentence is grammatically correct?

options.text: I not going to eat junk food.
I don't going to eat junk food.
I am not going to eat junk food.
I am going to not eat junk food.
options.feedback: Incorrect. "Not" should come after the verb "be".

questions.explanation:
The student analyzes the position of the negative particle "not" within the "be going to" structure.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence accurately describes their plans using "going to"?
questions.context:
Comparing two people's plans.
"Ana has her plane ticket to Cali. Luis says he might go to Cali but he doesn't have a ticket yet."

options.text: Ana is going to travel to Cali.
options.feedback: Correct! Having a ticket shows a definite plan/evidence.

options.text: Luis is going to travel to Cali.
options.feedback: Incorrect. He only "might" go; it's not a definite plan yet.

options.text: Both are going to travel to Cali.
options.feedback: Incorrect. Only Ana has a confirmed plan.
Incorrect. Ana is definitely planning to.

questions.explanation:
The student analyzes the level of certainty and evidence in the text to correctly use "going to" for the person with the definite plan.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: What is the best evaluation of this student's intentions?
questions.context:
Evaluating a student's resolution.
"I am going to start my homework earlier every day. I am also going to ask my teacher more questions. I want to improve my grades this term."

options.text: The student is lazy and wants more help.
options.feedback: Incorrect. Asking questions and starting earlier shows initiative.

options.text: The student has a proactive plan to achieve better academic results.
options.feedback: Correct! Both intentions (starting earlier and asking questions) are proactive steps toward the goal.

options.text: The student is going to fail because they have too many plans.
options.feedback: Incorrect. The plans are realistic and positive.

options.text: The student only cares about asking questions.
options.feedback: Incorrect. They also plan to start homework earlier.

questions.explanation: The student evaluates a set of future intentions to determine the underlying attitude and goal of the speaker.
